advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the _completion_precheck docstring 'THIRD CASE' to reflect fc20: administrative dispositions on any ticket type, including the reason-only (obsolete/wontfix) mint with no replacement.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:522: `` ``escalated`` while naming a live replacement) skips the billable verifier``

Behavior now: `_administrative_disposition` routes reason-only classes (obsolete/wontfix) and non-bug administrative closes through the signed path (close_precheck.py:469-494), which the docstring does not reflect.
advisory.finding: The _completion_precheck docstring's 'THIRD CASE' still describes the disposition path as 'a bug closed duplicate / not_a_bug / escalated while naming a live replacement', but ticket fc20 widened it to any ticket type via ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES and added the reason-only (obsolete/wontfix) mint that names no replacement. The documented return contract now mis-describes which closes take the signed-disposition branch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Amend lines 520-529 to say the disposition path covers administrative classes on any ticket type — replacement-bearing (duplicate/superseded) OR reason-only (obsolete/wontfix) — not just a bug naming a live replacement.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a forced library close (rebar.transition with force/force_close) carrying obsolete/wontfix + reason does NOT persist close_reason.
evidence: Library non-force arms covered: test_administrative_close_dispositions.py:259 (wrong class discards) and :289 (right class persists), both without force.

Forced administrative close covered only via CLI: test_administrative_close_dispositions.py:242 `test_forced_administrative_close_accepts_force_reason_as_justification` uses `_close(...)` = transition_cli, not rebar.transition.
ABSENCE: no `rebar.transition(..., close_class='obsolete', reason='x', force=True|force_close=...)` test asserting close_reason is absent.
advisory.finding: The forced-library-path close_reason discard is untested: _lib_writes.admits_close_reason includes a `not (force or force_close)` arm, so a FORCED library close (rebar.transition with force/force_close) carrying obsolete/wontfix + reason must NOT persist close_reason. No test exercises the force arm through rebar.transition; the forced administrative-close discard is verified only via transition_cli.
scenarios: A change drops the `not (force or force_close)` guard in _lib_writes; a forced library obsolete/wontfix close silently persists close_reason, drifting the library path from the CLI.
In-process (Tier E) callers force-close with a reason-required class and reason, unexpectedly recording close_reason alongside force_close_reason.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test calling rebar.transition(tid,'in_progress','closed',reason='x',close_class='obsolete',force_close='override',repo_root=...) and assert 'close_reason' not in reduced state while force_close_reason is set.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm ndjson re-import and existing callers passing a non-administrative --class on a non-bug close are not broken by the new close_class_refusal narrowing (import_ndjson.py should drop/normalize non-administrative close_class for non-bug records, or the guard should tolerate legacy replay).
evidence: Old guard was bug-only: diff removes `if target_status == "closed" and ticket_type == "bug" and not from_idea:` and replaces it with `refusal = close_class_refusal(...)` running on every close type (src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:302-320)

close_class is folded into state for ANY ticket type on close: `if target_status == "closed" and close_class: status_data["close_class"] = close_class` (src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:343) — so a non-bug ticket could previously carry an arbitrary close_class in reduced state

Held-out test only pins that a non-bug closes WITHOUT --class; it never covered a non-bug close carrying an arbitrary --class, which the old code accepted: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_bug_close_class_heldout.py:56-64

Consumer that re-feeds recorded close_class for any type into the stricter guard: `cc = str(rec.get("close_class") or "")` then `transition_compute(local, "open", "closed", force=True, close_class=close_class, ...)` (src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py:362, 374-375); comment claims 'Non-bug closes ignore close_class, so leave it empty for them' but the code does not empty it for non-bugs (import_ndjson.py:361-364)
dropped.finding: txn.close_class_refusal now rejects a non-administrative --class on non-bug closes, narrowing input that transition_core previously accepted (the old guard only fired for ticket_type=='bug', and close_class was folded into state for ANY ticket type). This is a backward-compat narrowing on the public `transition` CLI / rebar.transition() library surface, and the ndjson import replay path passes a record's recorded close_class through for any ticket type into the now-stricter guard, so re-importing a non-bug ticket previously closed with a non-administrative class (e.g. --class=regression) is now refused.
scenarios: A user re-imports (rebar import) a store where a task/story/epic was previously closed with a non-administrative --class value; the replay close is now refused by close_class_refusal and, via the fail-open at import_ndjson.py:377-378, the ticket is left non-closed with only a warning.
A library/automation caller of rebar.transition(<non-bug>, ..., close_class='regression') that previously succeeded now raises CommandError.
dropped.suggested_fix: In import_ndjson.py make the comment true — clear close_class for non-bug records (or map an out-of-vocabulary non-bug close_class to empty) before the replay transition_compute, so historical closes still round-trip.

A bug forced-closed with --class=regression begins receiving a misleading 'close it as a disposition' hint.
